text:
anika: quick heads-up — ran a small-batch FP8 canary across h100 + l40s. seeing a tiny but consistent perplexity drift after ~2k tokens on orion-13b-fp8-shadow (batch=4). not huge but it's reproducible :thinking_face:

ben: how small is "small-batch" here? and is it only on longseqs?

anika: batch=4, seq=2048, prefix-heavy prompt set (few-shot). spot-checks with batch=1 and batch=8 look fine. the pattern: accuracy holds for first ~1800 tokens then slowly diverges vs fp16 baseline.

luca: hmm could be kv-cache tiling handshake + fp8 accumulator rounding. did you test with kv-cache disabled?

anika: yes — reran with `--kv-cache=off` and the drift disappears. so definitely kv interaction.

maya: any perf tradeoffs with kv off? might not be acceptable for production.

anika: perf worse (~12% tail latency increase on h100), but stable.

ben: can you paste the minimal repro command and a short log snippet?

anika: repro: ```
run_canary --model orion-13b --quant fp8 --tiling auto --batch 4 --seq 2048 --prompts prompts/long-pref.json --canary-tag smallbatch-kv
```
log excerpt: ```
[2025-11-03T14:21:05Z] step 1900 token=1901 perplexity=12.3
[2025-11-03T14:21:08Z] step 1950 token=1951 perplexity=12.8  <-- diverging
[2025-11-03T14:21:12Z] step 2000 token=2001 perplexity=13.1
```

luca: that aligns with a rolling kv-tiling misalignment we've seen when runqueue switches precision mid-epoch. do you have kernel selection logs? `RUNTIME_KERNEL=info` should show fp8 vs fp16 handshake.

anika: added kernel logs — saw a fallback from fp8-tiling->fp16-tiling around token 1860 on one shard, while others stayed fp8. so mixed-precision mid-sequence across shards.

maya: so some shards are returning fp16 results while others stay fp8 -> mismatch in accumulators/scale factors. that would explain drift. canary should detect this automatically but apparently our detector only checks final outputs.

ben: is this H100-only or L40S too?

anika: both. h100 more likely because of aggressive kernel packing; l40s showed the same pattern but later and less frequently.

luca: root cause candidate: kernel handshake heuristic that chooses tiling based on instantaneous occupancy + remaining sequence length. with small batches and long sequences, some shards cross a threshold mid-run and swap kernels. the fp8 quant scaling isn't being reconciled across the swap.

maya: possible mitigations: 1) force tiling stable for full sequence (`--tiling=static`) 2) enforce uniform precision handshake before generation starts (preferable) 3) add runtime check to abort if kernel variant swaps mid-seq.

anika: tried `--tiling=static` — drift gone, tail latency ~+3% vs kv-off but much better than kv-off.

sre-oncall: deploy-bot scheduled a canary job yesterday: deploy-bot: "Canary job 2025-11-03T13:00 applied orion-13b fp8-smallbatch on shard set 7"

ben: what's the plan for rollout? do we need a hotfix kernel or can we relax handshake heuristics?

luca: patch plan: (a) short-term: add a safety that pins kernel selection per-request once first kernel chosen (config flag `pin_kernel=true`). (b) mid-term: reconcile fp8 scale states on kernel transition (harder). (c) long-term: update kernel selector to be sequence-aware for small-batch longseq workloads.

maya: can we ship (a) quickly as a runtime flag so Dedicated customers can opt-in? add to Dedicated config and expose in console. Need a one-line release note.

anika: I'll draft a release note and a canary checklist. minimal rollback plan: revert `pin_kernel` default if latency unacceptable.

ben: add alerting: create a guardrail that fires if token-level perplexity delta > 1.5 between p50 and baseline for 3 consecutive runs. include model/version and tiling flag in alert payload.

luca: add to runbook: commands to reproduce, how to toggle `pin_kernel`, and how to compare `kv-cache=off` vs `on` results. also include kernel logs grep: `grep KERNEL_SELECT /var/log/runtime.log`

anika: draft runbook snippet: ```
# toggle pin
redwood-runtimectl set global.pin_kernel=true
# repro
run_canary --model orion-13b --quant fp8 --tiling auto --batch 4 --seq 2048 --prompts prompts/long-pref.json
# kernel logs
grep KERNEL_SELECT /var/log/runtime.log | tail -n 50
```

maya: thanks. can we also add a quick eval comparing GPTQ and AWQ for this model on long-prefix prompts? maybe fp8 fragility differs.

anika: yes, I'll queue AWQ/GPTQ runs next week. initial thought: AWQ may be more robust on longprefix because it avoids per-kernel scaling handshake, but need data.

ben: assign owners: anika -> hotfix + canary; luca -> selector patch spec; maya -> console toggle + release note; ben -> alerting + runbook updates.

sre-oncall: noted, will watch canary metrics; ping @sre-oncall if any latency SLOs degrade. :white_check_mark:

anika: will post summary + link to artifacts when runs finish. thanks all. :raised_hands:
